narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The storyteller of Genesis; even, unhurried.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking to the patriarchs; majestic, promising.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.note: Son of Abraham; aged, blind and trembling in the blessing scene, peaceable among the Philistines.

abimelech.name: Abimelech
abimelech.note: King of the Palestines at Gerara; indignant, then seeking a treaty.

herdsmen-of-gerara.name: Herdsmen of Gerara
herdsmen-of-gerara.note: Local herdsmen quarrelling with Isaac's men over a well.

1.t: And when a famine came in the land, after that barrenness which had happened in the days of Abraham, Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Palestines, to Gerara.

2.t: And the Lord appeared to him, and said:
Go not down into Egypt, but stay in the land that I shall tell thee.

3.t: And sojourn in it, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee: for to thee and to thy seed I will give all these countries, to fulfil the oath which I swore to Abraham thy father.

4.t: And I will multiply thy seed like the stars of heaven: and I will give to thy posterity all these countries: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.

5.t: Because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my precepts and commandments, and observed my ceremonies and laws.

7.t: And when he was asked by the men of that place, concerning his wife, he answered:
for he was afraid to confess that she was his wife, thinking lest perhaps they would kill him because of her beauty.

8.t: And when very many days were passed, and he abode there, Abimelech, king of the Palestines, looking out through a window, saw him playing with Rebecca, his wife.

9.t: And calling for him, he said:
It is evident she is thy wife: why didst thou feign her to be thy sister?
I feared lest I should die for her sake.

10.t: Why hast thou deceived us? Some man of the people might have lain with thy wife, and thou hadst brought upon us a great sin.
And he commanded all the people, saying:

11.t: He that shall touch this man's wife, shall surely be put to death.

12.t: And Isaac sowed in that land, and he found that same year a hundredfold: and the Lord blessed him.

13.t: And the man was enriched, and he went on prospering and increasing, till he became exceeding great.

14.t: And he had possessions of sheep and of herds, and a very great family. Wherefore the Palestines envying him,

15.t: Stopped up at that time all the wells, that the servants of his father, Abraham, had digged, filling them up with earth:

16.t: Insomuch that Abimelech himself said to Isaac:
Depart from us, for thou art become much mightier than we.

17.t: So he departed, and came to the torrent of Gerara, to dwell there:

18.t: And he digged again other wells, which the servants of his father, Abraham, had digged, and which, after his death, the Philistines had of old stopped up: and he called them by the same names, by which his father before had called them.

19.t: And they digged in the torrent, and found living water:

20.t: But there also the herdsmen of Gerara strove against the herdsmen of Isaac, saying:
Wherefore he called the name of the well, on occasion of that which had happened, Calumny.

21.t: And they digged also another; and for that they quarrelled likewise, and he called the name of it, Enmity.

22.t: Going forward from thence, he digged another well, for which they contended not; therefore he called the name thereof, Latitude, saying:
Now hath the Lord given us room, and made us to increase upon the earth.

23.t: And he went up from that place to Bersabee,

24.t: Where the Lord appeared to him that same night, saying:
I am the God of Abraham thy father, do not fear, for I am with thee: I will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.

25.t: And he built there an altar: and called upon the name of the Lord, and pitched his tent; and commanded his servants to dig a well.

26.t: To which place when Abimelech, and Ochozath his friend, and Phicol chief captain of his soldiers, came from Gerara,

27.t: Why are ye come to me, a man whom you hate, and have thrust out from you?

28.t: We saw that the Lord is with thee, and therefore we said: Let there be an oath between us, and let us make a covenant,
28.q: "They answered": Abimelech with Ochozath and Phicol; given to Abimelech as their spokesman rather than a group voice

29.t: That thou do us no harm, as we on our part have touched nothing of thine, nor have done any thing to hurt thee; but with peace have sent thee away, increased with the blessing of the Lord.
29.q: "They answered": Abimelech with Ochozath and Phicol; given to Abimelech as their spokesman rather than a group voice

30.t: And he made them a feast, and after they had eaten and drunk:

31.t: Arising in the morning, they swore one to another: and Isaac sent them away peaceably to their own home.

32.t: And behold, the same day the servants of Isaac came, telling him of a well which they had digged, and saying:

33.t: Whereupon he called it Abundance: and the name of the city was called Bersabee, even to this day.

34.t: And Esau being forty years old, married wives, Judith, the daughter of Beeri, the Hethite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon, of the same place.

35.t: And they both offended the mind of Isaac and Rebecca.
